notes:
The section heading is "EAST COAST OF SCOTLAND." (line 269), with the sub-heading "EAST OF SCOTLAND." (line 274). Inside that, rows are grouped under "Shetland." (284), "Orkney." (291) and "Mainland." (301). The coast field uses those three group names. There are 28 stations, numbered 4–29 plus 26B and 28B. No keepers are named: line 276 says the reporters' names are given under "Diary from the Stations", which starts at line 324 (e.g. John Nichol at N. Unst).

How I recorded things:
- Fragments are each line exactly as printed, with only the leading indentation removed. Internal spacing is kept, including the double space in "Dunnet Head,  Caithness,".
- In number, I dropped the period that follows each printed number ("4." becomes "4"; "26B." becomes "26B").
- Names keep the trailing comma as printed. The county or locality goes in place, without its trailing comma.
- The column headers are not printed on each row. So in other I added labels ("Schedules filled in 1887", "Returns in 9 years incl. 1887", "Value", "Feet") in front of the values, which are copied exactly as printed. The header's own wording is "In 1887. Schedules filled in." / "Returns in 9 years including 1887." / "1887. Actual returns." / "Values." / "Feet." I assigned values to columns by where they sit on the line.
- The * is the only mark, and it is in the "1887. Actual returns." column. Its horizontal position varies a little from row to row.
- The character column is "Values." (Roman numerals I–V), not a description of the light, so character is null throughout and the value is in other.

Things to be careful with:
- Several rows have figures in the "Returns in 9 years" column but no "Schedules" figure. I read those single figures by position: Auskerry 6, Cromarty 6, Chanonry Point 4, Girdleness 1st and Fidra 2 are all returns counts. Fidra's 2 is odd for a station "instituted 1886", but it does fit 1886 and 1887.
- Buchan Ness and Girdleness show "1st" in the returns column, which seems to mean their first year of returns.
- Bell Rock's schedules entry is "1 (one lost)". Isle of May has 0 schedules and no *.
- The rows for Sumburgh Head and all of Orkney have no height in feet.
- Carr Rock (26B) and Fidra (28B) each wrap onto two lines (315–316 and 319–320), and both have "?" for Value and Feet. Fidra's place "Firth of / Forth" is split across the two lines. "instituted 1886" is printed in Fidra's row, so I put it in other.
- Carr Rock's type is printed as "Lightship", not "L.V.". It is the only row with a type; the lighthouses have none.

Kept as printed, though they look wrong:
- "Whalsey Skerries": the usual spelling is Whalsay.
- "N. Ronaldshay"
- "Holborn Head": not Holburn.
- "Girdleness" and "Montroseness" are each one word.
- "Montroseness, Aberdeen": Scurdie Ness/Montrose is in Forfarshire, not Aberdeen.
- "Chanonry Point, Elgin": Chanonry is in Ross-shire.
- "Bell Rock, Fife Coast": it lies off Forfarshire.
- "Cromarty, East Cromarty"
- "Tarbat Ness, East Ross"
- "St Abb's Head" has no period after "St".
